atomicity.reason: One obligation: the reported capacity figure never increases; the sentence about discarding higher measurements is the mechanism of that same rule.

comprehensibility.reason: Intelligible on its own: the body gives the unit (percentage of rated capacity), the rule (never increases), the discard behaviour and the purpose (a worn pack must not look healthier than it was).

feasibility.reason: A monotonic running-minimum clamp on a reported figure is trivial to implement and contradicts nothing in the linked context.

parent_fit.reason: Implements the parent's explicit observable: the fleet report shows a remaining-capacity figure that never rises over the life of the pack.

unambiguity.reason: 'Remaining capacity expressed as a percentage of rated capacity' is almost the wording REQ_SOC_ACCURACY uses to define state of charge (the share of rated capacity still available); only the cues 'never increase' and 'worn pack' show that capacity fade is meant, not SoC.
unambiguity.suggestion: Use a distinct term (e.g. state of health or capacity retention) or define 'remaining capacity' as the pack's full-charge capacity relative to rated capacity.

verifiability.reason: Concrete property check: supply capacity candidates above and below the reported value (including across power cycles) and confirm the reported series never increases and higher candidates leave it unchanged.

summary: Clearly traceable and testable monotonic-capacity rule; unambiguity reduced because 'remaining capacity' collides with the SoC definition used by REQ_SOC_ACCURACY.
